graph.summary: Metoprolol → Beta-1 adrenergic receptor → cardiac muscle hypertrophy → Heart failure

evidence.snippet: Most of these effects were reduced in BNP-Sham and PMI mice by the selective β1-adrenergic blocker metoprolol.
evidence.explanation: Identifies metoprolol as a selective β1-adrenergic blocker, i.e. it decreases the activity of the beta-1 adrenergic receptor.

paper.title: Functional evidence for an active role of B-type natriuretic peptide in cardiac remodelling and pro-arrhythmogenicity.

evidence.snippet: Metoprolol tartrate, a β1-receptor blocker with a short half-life and low oral bioavailability, was selected as the model drug.
evidence.explanation: Confirms metoprolol's mechanism class as a β1-receptor blocker (antagonist), decreasing beta-1 adrenergic receptor activity.

paper.title: Design and evaluation of a novel expandable gastroretentive film for sustained Metoprolol release.

evidence.snippet: The present study tested the hypothesis that sympathetic-mediated hypertrophy of neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes (NRVMs) translated to an increase in calcium influx secondary to the upregulation of CaV1.2 channel subunits.
evidence.explanation: Sympathetic (catecholamine/β1-adrenergic) stimulation of ventricular cardiomyocytes drives a hypertrophic response, i.e. β1-adrenergic receptor signaling positively regulates cardiac muscle hypertrophy.

paper.title: Sympathetic Stimulation Upregulates the Ca2+ Channel Subunit, CaVα2δ1, via the β1 and ERK 1/2 Pathway in Neonatal Ventricular Cardiomyocytes.

evidence.snippet: Confocal imaging of norepinephrine (NE)-treated NRVMs revealed a hypertrophic response compared to untreated NRVMs.
evidence.explanation: Norepinephrine acting through the β1-adrenergic receptor produces a hypertrophic response in ventricular cardiomyocytes, evidencing positive regulation of cardiac muscle hypertrophy by β1-AR signaling.

paper.title: Sympathetic Stimulation Upregulates the Ca2+ Channel Subunit, CaVα2δ1, via the β1 and ERK 1/2 Pathway in Neonatal Ventricular Cardiomyocytes.

evidence.snippet: Overstimulation of the orthosympathetic system leads to cardiovascular cell and tissue damage through prolonged activation of β-1-2 adrenergic receptors (BARs).
evidence.explanation: Prolonged activation of β1 adrenergic receptors drives maladaptive cardiac tissue changes (including hypertrophy), supporting that β1-AR signaling positively regulates pathological cardiac muscle hypertrophy.

paper.title: Cardiac salvage by tweaking with beta-3-adrenergic receptors.

evidence.snippet: Chronic activation of the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) contributes to cardiac remodeling and the transition to heart failure (HF).
evidence.explanation: Pathological cardiac muscle hypertrophy is the central maladaptive component of cardiac remodeling; chronic sympathetic-driven remodeling contributes to the transition to heart failure.

paper.title: Renal denervation mitigates cardiac remodeling and renal damage in Dahl rats: a comparison with β-receptor blockade.
paper.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension

evidence.snippet: Elevated BNP levels, by inducing sympathetic overdrive and altering Ca(2+) handling, promote adverse cardiac remodelling and VAs, which could account in part for the progression of HF after MI.
evidence.explanation: Adverse cardiac remodelling (of which pathological muscle hypertrophy is the core process) contributes to the progression of heart failure.

paper.title: Functional evidence for an active role of B-type natriuretic peptide in cardiac remodelling and pro-arrhythmogenicity.
